findings.text: Provides priority inheritance lock acquisition for a user address with shared or private scope, supporting blocking wait with absolute timeout, immediate try, and retry after transient contention or user fault.

Provides priority inheritance unlock for a user address, enforcing that only the recorded owner may release and supporting handoff to a kernel waiter versus release of an uncontended value, plus a robust variant that clears pending robust state on success.

Provides reconciliation between user value and kernel inheritance state after an acquisition attempt, covering acquired, stolen and contended outcomes with success, held indication or error propagation.
Provides real time mutex proxy operations for futex use, comprising nonblocking attempt, proxy start with chain walk, interruptible proxy wait, and proxy cleanup that resolves steal races.
Provides movement of a queued waiter between hash buckets under a new key and completion of wakeup for a waiter that was requeued onto inheritance state.

Hash bucket lock precedes inheritance mutex wait lock; handoff sequences ensure observation of new waiters by holding one across the transition, and fault or reschedule paths drop both before reacquiring in bucket then wait order with revalidation.

Owner repair requires the queue lock held by the caller and acquires the inheritance wait lock with interrupts disabled; the nested acquisition is released to resolve user faults or rescheduling before rechecking ownership.
Proxy start requires wait lock held and performs immediate take attempt before chain walk; proxy wait and cleanup manage interrupt disabling and waiter indication repair around sleep and removal.

Unlock rejects callers whose thread identifier differs from the user value and rejects kernel state where inheritance owner differs from current or is missing when waiters claim presence, treating user values as untrusted.

User value repair preserves the died indication while installing the new owner identifier together with the waiters indication, adding died indication when kernel owner is absent and repeating compare exchange until the observed value is stable.

Uncontended unlock attempts transition of the user value to zero and reports contention when concurrent modification is observed; contended unlock discards stale kernel waiters lacking real time waiters and rescans for a live top waiter.

Acquisition maps disabled inheritance support, cache refill failure, failed immediate try, interruption and timeout or signal outcomes to distinct caller errors, waits for an exiting owner to avoid live lock, and retries private versus shared keys appropriately after faults.

Requeue across buckets transfers waiter accounting and queue lock association only when bucket chains differ while always adopting the new key; requeue wake unqueues, detaches real time waiter linkage, refreshes key and lock association, records locked completion and wakes the task.
Default waiter template defines a wake callback, an empty key, a match any bitset and an idle requeue state, with list linkage established at queue time rather than in the template.

Requeue coordination progresses among idle, ignore, in progress, wait, done and locked conditions, where preparation refuses ignored waiters, completion records success or deadlock with early wakeup interaction, and synchronous wakeup either observes completion or parks until progress finishes.
External call sites expose inheritance lock acquisition with flags, timeout and try selection, and inheritance unlock with flags and optional robust clearing, operating on user addresses.

Concurrent steal, exit, hash resize, early wakeup and user modification can skew hash bucket, inheritance state, real time waiter list and user value views, requiring ownership revalidation, retry and discard of departing waiters without false missing of arrivals.

Unresolvable user access leaves user state immutable while kernel inheritance owner is forced to match real time mutex owner; the resulting divergence is expected to cause later unlock rejection under inheritance consistency rules.

Q_REQUEUE_PI_NONE equals zero while Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE equals one while Q_REQUEUE_PI_IN_PROGRESS equals two while Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT equals three while Q_REQUEUE_PI_DONE equals four while Q_REQUEUE_PI_LOCKED equals five.
